findings.title: website_name leaks restricted website data for untrusted users
findings.body: The serializer adds website_name as a public attribute, but website is listed in untrusted_attributes and is hidden when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) applies (for example, a TL0 user viewed anonymously). website_name is derived from the same hidden website value and has no equivalent restriction, so it can expose the user's website host/path even when website itself must not be serialized. It should be treated as untrusted or its inclusion should enforce the same restriction as website.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the required question mark
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializer uses include_<attribute>? methods to decide whether an attribute should be serialized. The added method is named include_website_name instead of include_website_name?, so it will never be called. The intended guard based on website.present? is ineffective, and website_name may be serialized unconditionally, including when it is nil or should be omitted.

findings.title: tests do not cover website_name restriction for untrusted users
findings.body: The untrusted-attribute spec lists website but not the newly added website_name, and there is no test asserting that website_name is omitted when a TL0 user is viewed anonymously. Since website_name reveals the same information as website, this missing coverage allows the privacy regression to pass tests.

findings.title: hostname comparison can treat unrelated sites as the same domain
findings.body: The same-domain heuristic strips the first hostname label and compares the remainder, and also uses simple suffix matching. This can classify unrelated hosts that share a parent domain as the same site, such as myforum.github.io and someuser.github.io, causing the full website path to be shown when only the hostname should be shown. A more precise same-site check is needed.
